ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

Baseten's engineers want to work in an AI-first way. What's missing isn't enthusiasm — it's the platform underneath it. Today everyone assembles their own agent config, context files, and MCP servers, so the good patterns stay trapped in individual setups instead of becoming defaults everyone inherits.

You'll build that platform: the agent configurations tuned to our monorepo, the context and tooling layer that makes agents competent in our codebase, the evals that tell us which approaches actually work, and the rollout mechanics that get a new engineer productive with agents in week one.

You are not here to mandate how engineers use AI — you're here to make the good path the easy path. Success looks like teams adopting what you build because it beats what they'd cobble together themselves, not because a policy requires it. Platform engineer, not AI evangelist. Ship infrastructure, measure it, kill what doesn't work, let adoption be the referee.

The playbook for AI-first SDLC doesn't exist at any company yet. You'll write ours.

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

Agent substrate — Repo-level context infrastructure that makes agents competent in our codebase (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md http://CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions, architecture and domain context, and the tooling to keep it accurate as code moves). Internal MCP servers giving agents scoped access to CI, observability, incident tooling, deployment state, and docs. Shared skills, subagents, and hooks that encode Baseten workflows. Sandboxed environments where agents can build and test safely.

The golden path — Project templates and onboarding that ship with AI tooling configured and working. Self-serve infrastructure so teams build their own agents without you as the bottleneck. Gateway, auth, cost controls, and audit logging for internal model access.

The feedback loop — Eval harnesses that answer "is this config better than that one" against real Baseten tasks, not vibes. Instrumentation of AI tool usage and its downstream effects on cycle time, review latency, and change failure rate. Honest reporting, including on what you built that didn't pan out.

Agents in the SDLC — Automation where agents earn their keep: PR review triage, test gap-filling, incident context assembly, migrations and refactors, codebase Q&A. Integrating agents into CI/CD with guardrails that make it trustworthy.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the internal AI developer platform end to end — architecture, build, rollout, operation, measurement.

 - Evaluate and integrate third-party AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and whatever ships next quarter), and build the context layer that makes them work against our monorepo.

 - Build frameworks that let other engineers create their own agents without deep LLM expertise.

 - Establish the evaluation practice for AI-assisted development at Baseten, and use it to drive investment decisions.

 - Drive adoption through developer experience — good defaults, clear docs, low friction — not mandate.

 - Embed with teams to find where AI genuinely unblocks them, then generalize those wins into platform capabilities.

 - Own the safety layer: permissions, secrets handling, audit trails, cost management.
   
   

REQUIREMENTS

 - Have 4+ years of relevant industry experience building and enabling AI native SDLC

 - Strong proficiency in Python and/or Go, building tools other engineers depend on daily.

 - Hands-on experience with LLMs and agent frameworks — tool calling, MCP, context management, orchestration, failure handling. You've shipped something agentic that real people used, not just prototyped.

 - Deep personal fluency with AI coding tools and well-formed opinions about where they break down.

 - Platform mindset: you build for adoption and self-service, treat internal engineers as customers, and would rather ship a good default than write a style guide.

 - Developer tooling, CI/CD, and Kubernetes/Docker fundamentals.

 - Comfort with ambiguity — this space invalidates its own best practices every few months.

 - Excellent written communication. Much of your leverage is docs, templates, and examples that scale beyond conversations you're in.

BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

A profitable DTC pet brand is looking for a Head of Retention & Customer Experience to join our team! You will own everything after the first order: subscriptions, email and SMS, the post-purchase journey and customer experience, across both of our brands.
 We're doing $50M+ a year and scaling to $100M+, and we want one senior leader who owns retention A-Z: lower churn, significantly higher lifetime value and a better customer experience across the board. We are looking to hire someone with 5-6+ years in retention or lifecycle at DTC brands, who has led retention at a subscription brand doing $30-50M+ a year (ideally nine figures). The ideal candidate is hands-on in Klaviyo and Loop (or similar), has led a retention and customer experience team, and has managed agencies.
 The mission of this role 
 Own retention A-Z to fuel the growth to 9-figures. This role comes in to drive three things: lower churn, significantly higher lifetime value, and a better customer experience across the board. Success is lower churn, stronger retention, much higher lifetime value, more revenue from email and SMS, and happier customers.
 Who are we? 
 We are a profitable DTC brand selling premium pet products. We sell across Shopify, Amazon and Chewy, and we're one of the fastest-growing brands in the pet space – $50M+ in annual revenue and scaling to $100M+. We recently launched a second brand, expanding into a new customer base. We're a 100% remote, lean, senior team that moves fast, and every person here has a massive impact on the business.
 Better Everyday: have a retention test live every week across subscriptions, flows or the post-purchase experience, and write down what each result teaches.
 Speed Is King: spot a churn, refund or CSAT problem the day it shows up and have a fix in motion that week.
 Work Smart: AI and automation first. Claude reads cancellation reasons, reviews and tickets to find why customers leave, AI drafts flow copy and segments, and retention KPIs report themselves every week.
 Overdeliver: bring the CEO the next big retention lever before being asked, and get more lifetime value from every customer than the plan called for.
 If you want to challenge yourself and shape a fast-growing company, work directly with the founder, and play a big role in scaling it to $100M+... If you want to drive results with a group of passionate, smart, hardworking people, in an environment without politics or corporate chicanery, being hands-on and active – then you've come to the right place.
 Outcomes (what success looks like) 
 Churn goes down: monthly subscription churn and save rate, by brand
 Retention improves: repeat purchase rate and cohort retention at 3, 6 and 12 months
 Lifetime value rises significantly: 12-month lifetime value by cohort and brand vs the same cohorts last year
 Email and SMS drive more revenue: email and SMS share of total revenue, and revenue per recipient
 Customers are happier across the board: CSAT, review rating, refund rate and tickets per order
 Key Objectives 
 Own the subscription program for both brands: offers, cadence, bundles, the customer portal and the cancellation flow.
 Build and test save offers, skip, swap and pause options, and win-back flows to cut churn.
 Own email and SMS strategy for both brands, and manage the retention agency's calendar, flows, targets and results.
 Build the lifecycle journey from first order to loyal customer: welcome, post-purchase, replenishment, cross-sell, win-back and VIP flows.
 Map and improve the full post-purchase journey, and run a loyalty, referral or VIP program if the numbers support it.
 Lead the customer experience team and set customer service policy that protects both the customer and the margin.
 Report cohort retention and lifetime value against target every month, and name the biggest lever.
 Fully remote, based outside the US.
 Fluent in English.
 Retention Leadership: 5-6+ years in retention or lifecycle at DTC brands, including leading retention at a subscription brand doing $30-50M+ a year (ideally nine figures). This is a must.
 Subscription Expertise: you have grown a subscription program and know churn, saves, cohorts and MRR inside out.
 Lifecycle Marketing: you build email and SMS programs (Klaviyo or similar) that drive a large share of revenue without burning the list.
 Tools: deep hands-on experience with Klaviyo (or similar) and Loop (or a similar subscription platform).
 Analytical: you read cohort, lifetime value and churn data fast and find the lever that moves the number.
 Testing Discipline: you run clear tests on offers, flows and save tactics, and read results honestly.
 Leadership: you have led a retention and customer experience team, including managing agencies, through KPIs and goals.
 Commercial Judgement: you protect margin, and know when a discount or save offer earns its cost.
 Customer obsessed: you understand why customers stay or leave, and fix the cause, not the symptom.
 Accountabilities 
 Subscriptions and churn: own the subscription program for both brands, keep at least one save or retention test live every week, grow the share of new customers who subscribe (working with the CRO Lead on on-site and post-purchase offers), and report subscribers, MRR, churn and save rate by brand every week.
 Email, SMS and lifecycle: own email and SMS strategy, manage the retention agency, keep the calendar live and flows in testing, keep list health and deliverability strong, and plan sale and launch campaigns with the Head of Growth and the Head of Brand & Community.
 Post-purchase experience and loyalty: ship at least one post-purchase improvement every month, and use cancellation reasons, reviews, surveys and support contact reasons to find why customers leave and fix the cause with the owning team.
 Customer experience and support: lead the Customer Experience Manager, own the weekly CX KPI scorecard (CSAT, first response time, AI resolution rate, refund rate and chargebacks), set customer service policy, and grow 4- and 5-star reviews.
 Retention data and reporting: track cohort retention, repeat purchase rate and lifetime value by brand and channel, report retention KPIs weekly, run a monthly retention review with the CEO, and write the retention playbook as SOPs so it runs without one person.
 How Our Hiring Works & How We Operate 
 (1) Application + Screening Interview
 (2) In-Depth Interview with our CEO
 (3) Reference Calls
 (4) Final Interview with our CEO
 Salary Expectation 
 USD $115,000 to $145,000 a year (based on experience and expertise) + performance bonus of 15-20% of base after the trial period.

ABOUT PHOENIX

À PROPOS DE PHOENIX

Fondée en 2019, Phoenix bâtit la plateforme de télésanté la plus fiable au Canada, avec la mission de rendre les soins spécialisés accessibles à toute la population canadienne, peu importe où elle se trouve. Notre plateforme fait tomber les obstacles à l'accès aux soins et permet aux patients de prendre leur santé en main, grâce à des traitements personnalisés et à l'accompagnement de professionnels de la santé autorisés.

Si vous aimez voir les grandes idées se transformer en résultats concrets, vous allez vous plaire ici. Nous sommes une équipe de gens créatifs qui aiment résoudre des problèmes, qui avancent de façon réfléchie et qui travaillent ensemble en personne, parce que nous croyons que c'est comme ça que le meilleur travail se fait. Chez Phoenix, vous aurez de l'autonomie dans votre travail, des collègues qui tiennent au succès des autres, et une mission qui améliore concrètement les soins de santé au pays.

Votre rôle

Nous sommes une entreprise de télésanté qui met en relation des patients avec des professionnels de la santé autorisés, par l'intermédiaire d'une plateforme en ligne sécurisée et asynchrone. Nous recherchons une personne titulaire d'un permis d'IPS pour évaluer les demandes des patients, déterminer leur admissibilité au traitement et rédiger des ordonnances lorsque cela est cliniquement indiqué, sans aucune rencontre vidéo ou téléphonique en temps réel.

À PROPOS DE LA PLATEFORME

Les patients remplissent un questionnaire médical guidé qui couvre leurs antécédents. Vous examinez chaque dossier, généralement en moins de cinq minutes, puis vous déterminez la suite : approuver le traitement, demander des renseignements supplémentaires ou refuser. Toutes les communications avec les patients passent par la messagerie sécurisée intégrée à la plateforme.

PROBLÈMES DE SANTÉ ACTUELLEMENT TRAITÉS

 - Gestion du poids

 - Santé sexuelle (dysfonction érectile, éjaculation précoce)

 - Perte de cheveux

 - Hormonothérapie (testostérone)
   
   

RESPONSABILITÉS

 - Examiner les antécédents médicaux transmis par les patients et déterminer leur admissibilité au traitement

 - Rédiger les ordonnances lorsque cela est cliniquement indiqué, ou faire un suivi directement auprès des patients pour obtenir des renseignements supplémentaires

 - Communiquer avec les patients par messagerie sécurisée, au besoin

 - Collaborer avec les équipes clinique et produit afin d'améliorer les processus

 - Signaler les irritants dans l'expérience des patients ou des professionnels de la santé et travailler avec les équipes Expérience client, Produit et Développement pour les régler

 - Apporter un point de vue clinique sur les nouveaux problèmes de santé traités, les nouveaux protocoles et les lancements de produits, à mesure que la plateforme évolue
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - Être membre en règle de l'Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers du Québec (OIIQ) et détenir un certificat de spécialiste en soins de première ligne, avec admissibilité à un permis d'exercice dans d'autres provinces canadiennes (accompagnement offert pour l'obtention des permis, au besoin)

 - Aisance à travailler au sein d'une plateforme de soins numérique

 - Excellente communication écrite et capacité à travailler efficacement dans un environnement asynchrone, à rythme soutenu

 - Réactivité et empathie dans les interactions avec les patients

 - Intérêt à collaborer avec des équipes non cliniques

 - Expérience en santé des hommes, un atout
   

À QUOI S'ATTENDRE

 - Aucune rencontre en temps réel. Toutes les interactions avec les patients sont asynchrones : aucun appel ni aucune visioconférence à l'horaire.

 - Aucune facturation aux assureurs. Les patients paient directement : ni paperasse d'assurance, ni traitement de réclamations.

 - Assurance responsabilité professionnelle. Votre protection actuelle (assurance collective de l'OIIQ et adhésion à la SPIIC) s'applique ; aucune couverture supplémentaire n'est exigée.

 - Le travail clinique se fait entièrement à distance: aucun déplacement n'est requis pour ce rôle. Ce sont les équipes internes (Produit, Ingénierie, Opérations, Marketing, etc.) qui se réunissent à nos bureaux de Toronto pour la planification, la rétroaction et la résolution de problèmes.

OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

 

AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Float is building out its next stage of growth operations. As Revenue Operations Manager, you’ll own the systems, programs, and operating rhythms that take a prospect from first touch to active, spending customer.

You’ll build, not inherit. This role is for someone who gets excited about being a high impact individual contributor. You’ll partner with Sales, BDR, Partnerships, Marketing Ops, Finance, Product, and Customer Success leadership to turn strategy into repeatable programs that improve pipeline quality, conversion, and activation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and optimize the end-to-end sales-acquired customer journey. This starts with ISR/BDR (Team of 3) prospecting inbound and outbound, AE (Team of 10) sales funnel management and deal execution, customer activation (Team of 5) through first card usage (months 0–4).

 - Own pipeline health: coverage ratios, stage conversion, win/loss analysis

 - Build and own forecasting and quota-setting for sales-acquired TPV, and partner with Marketing Ops on the self-serve-to-sales handoff.

 - Build scalable territory and account-assignment programs for BDR/AE capacity.

 - Partner with BDR/AE leadership on reporting cadences, monetization levers (e.g. contract terms), operating rhythms, and performance metrics.

 - Own streamlining handoffs from Marketing > BDR, BDR > AE, and AE to Customer Activation teams

 - Translate fragmented pipeline and activation data into recommendations for Sales and GTM leadership.

 - Identify and automate manual BDR/AE work so reps spend more time selling.

 - 5+ years in Sales/Acquisition Ops, Revenue Ops, or similar with end-to-end ownership of a sales-acquired pipeline.

 - Experience in a consumption/usage-based business where activation, not just bookings, drives revenue is an asset

 - Proven track record building outbound and sales programs with measured impact on business outcomes (pipeline volume/quality, deal size, win rates, productivity)

 - Hands-on Salesforce and sales-engagement tooling experience.

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable turning fragmented data into a forecast leadership can trust.

 - You prefer inheriting a mature process over building it.

 - You do not want a high ownership role 

 - Your background is BDR/AE execution rather than owning the systems behind it.

 - You'd rather report on pipeline metrics than build what generates them.

OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

 - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

 - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose   
 This position holds responsibility for the delivery of all functional activities related to admissions processes. In this capacity the Admission Co-ordinator (AC) is trained to handle admissions processes and procedures. The incumbent works within a team of 10-12 people and may be assigned responsibility for various procedures related to communications with applicants seeking admission to the University. For example, the Admissions Co-ordinator is required to answer telephone, in person and email inquiries from applicants regarding the status of their admission file decision. The incumbent is required to track and communicate Ontario Secondary School (OSS) special case reviews that fall below normal admission requirements or do not follow normal OSS requirements.   
 Responsibility ranges from entry level admissions to a leadership role, leading process and procedural projects and providing the day to day leadership required to ensure all activities are maintained, while resolving more complex problems.   
 The AC advises and counsels applicants with respect to the implications of and reasons for positive and negative admission decisions. In doing so, he/she must be cognizant of the stresses and pressures that potential students and their guardians are experiencing and delicately handle very sensitive issues so as not to adversely affect the university’s enrolment targets and overall reputation. This requires both Faculty specific and systems specific knowledge, especially when dealing with the many cases that deviate from the norm.   
 The incumbent is responsible for verifying authenticity, coding and updating data received from or on behalf of applicants such as English Language Test scores, transcripts or other documents that are required before admission decisions can be finalized. As files are completed, the incumbent independently assesses when some applicant files are ready for a decision. In reviewing transcripts he/she is responsible in calculating routine overall grade point averages. As needed, the incumbent is required to code admission amendments to program evaluations as well as program status changes for the applicant.   
 QUEST (PeopleSoft Student Information System) and DMS (OnBase Document Management System) allows staff to track the status of documents received, correspondence, and generate letters and reports. Throughout the admissions cycle, the incumbent is expected to be able to answer inquires related to admissions decisions, offer conditions, for both OSS and specialty admissions groups (X+X, exchange, part-time, non-degree and extend learning students. The incumbent may have frequent contact with UWaterloo Staff and Faculty Admissions Officers to discuss the status of applicant files and communicate this information precisely and accurately. The AC is expected to run standard queries and extracts to identify the various stages of completion of admissions activities and error checking. The incumbent is required to have a thorough knowledge of business processes and practices to make suggestions for improvements and to identify discrepancies.   
 Challenges faced by the AC result from: the diversity of end users and system functionality used within the Office, as well as the need to keep abreast of admission requirements, policy and procedure changes being implemented within the Registrar’s Office and University and increase in volume during peak periods. Upgrades to QUEST and DMS systems often lead to changes in administrative processes and procedures.   
 Annually, more than 60,000 students apply for undergraduate studies at the University. The incumbent has responsibility for email, telephone and in-person support for undergraduate applicants. In addition, the incumbent is responsible for processing undergraduate applicant documents by established deadline dates.  
 Key Accountabilities   
 Evaluating & Communicating with Applicant   
 Acknowledge and respond to applicant inquiries regarding the status of their applications, interpretation of admission requirements and procedures   
 Problem-solve with respect to one-of-a-kind scenarios & tailors communication e.g. content style and medium, to diverse audiences  
 Act as a conduit between applicants and members of the Admissions Team  
 Execute decisions with respect to OSS applicant files  
 Assess and verify admission e-files with regard to OSS applicants; pre-assess acknowledge and prepare files for Part-time/Distance Education (PT/DE) applications for admissibility  
 Provide written and oral information regarding policies and procedures of the university to applicants and departmental staff and faculty as it relates to admissions   
 Complete student registration, including, but not limited to: add/drop activity, block enrolment, service indicators, term activation, unit load as this pertains to the Exchange and PT/DE  
 Determine and verify accuracy for coding of: English language test scores, transfer credits, transcript text, exchange applications, letters of permission, agent approvals  
 Review information and provide revisions to the appropriate member of the Admissions Team e.g. Updating information on Future Students website, reviewing content for Viewbooks  
 Report problems and issues to the Manager, Admissions Operations where current practice may not be to the best advantage of applicants. Provide viable solutions/suggestions for recommended change, where possible  
 Formulates optimal ways to improve service/program in the department, taking into account a longer-term and broader organization perspective   
 Liaise with the staff in Registrar’s Office; attend Admissions Team meetings and Recruitment Team meetings as required; keep abreast of policy and procedure changes being instituted  
 Provide on-going updates to the other members in the Customer Service team  
 Prepare Offer Package material (for release in paper format or electronically via email)  
 Works closely with The Centre staff to train and answer questions that pertain to applicant inquiries  
 Complexity of Admissions Co-ordinators Accountabilities is Demonstrated by the Following Examples:   
 Many of the coding situations handled by the incumbent, such as indexing, coding offers of admission, refusals, transfer credit coding, residency status, course registration, etc. affect the accuracy of Government reporting as well as tuition assessment   
 OSS disqualification: new grade information requires a review of grade averages. Errors in calculations can result in the revocation of an offer of admission, which in turn can result in damage to the institution’s reputation and loss of revenue  
 A student’s status may change term by term from full-time enrolment, to part-time, Letter of Permission, or an Exchange program. Departments such as Student Finance, Student Awards, Co-operative Education and Career Services and Undergraduate Offices rely on this information to trigger essential processes in their respective areas  
 Academic Advisement, Student Awards and Financial Aid, Student Accounts and Student Records are immediately impacted by admissions updates  
 Communication & Stakeholder Focus:   
 The incumbent will respond to inquiries from applicants, UWaterloo Staff and Faculty Undergraduate Advisors regarding the status of an applicant’s file   
 The incumbent will provide additional support to the Customer Service Team that is the student’s first line of contact when visiting the Registrar’s Office. S/he will be expected to answer inquiries and deal with applicant directly to explain policies and procedures  
 Pre-Assessment of Applicant Files:   
 PT/DE applicant files are pre-assessed for completeness and recommendations are shared with the Non-OSS Admission Officer  
 Post Degree and in-coming Letter of Permission (LoP) applicant files are assessed and decisions communicated directly to the applicant  
 Exchange files are pre-assessed for completeness and forwarded for review and decision to the appropriate faculty representative  
 Athlete files are closely monitored, pre-assessed and passed to the AR for review and decision in a timely manner while working closely with the Athletics Director  
 Document Management System (DMS):   
 Query on student files for decisions, document checks as well as OUAC details  
 Accurately match all documents received to student files, re-index unmatched documents or errors  
 Index (paper and e-batches) to applicant file  
 Indexing of electronic IELTS results   
 Identify discrepancies and communicate these to the Admissions Systems team  
 Complete quality assurance checks on all indexed documents  
 Reporting:  
 Run standard queries to gather data from the Student Information System (PeopleSoft/QUEST) & Document Management System (DMS) to identify the various stages of completion of admissions activities  
 Required to have a thorough knowledge of business processes and practices to accurately identify discrepancies or anomalies  
 Recruitment and Admissions Activities:  
 Opportunity to participate in the 3-day Ontario Universities’ Fair that takes place annually in Toronto  
 Opportunity to participate in on-campus events such as March Open House, You@Waterloo Day, and other recruitment-related activities  
 Aids in the training of Liaison travelers and student ambassadors  
 Undertake research and specialized projects or coding as determined by the Manager, Admissions or Associate Registrar Admissions   
 Aids in the administration of certain office wide responsibilities including: examinations, convocation and such general and specific duties as may from time to time be determined  
 Required Qualifications   
 Education

 Previous customer service experience required  
 Experience

 Experience dealing with stakeholders and/or educational organizations  
 Previous administrative experience an asset

 Experience with Microsoft Excel

 Experience with Microsoft Access is an asset  
 Experience using online Student Information Systems and DMS is an asset

 Lead the team

Own the platform

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product managers who bring exceptional creative, strategic, and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company's vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate Product Managers to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry.
 Pricing is the primary economic engine of Lyft's marketplace — a high-precision, real-time system that processes millions of fare calculations per hour, balancing rider affordability, driver earnings, and Lyft's sustainable growth. The Pricing team sits at the intersection of the marketplace, mediating between rider demand and driver supply, and is a core pillar of the Rider Organization.
 The Base Pricing Team owns the systems that set the base price of a Lyft ride for every ride type, region, and ride intent. Behind these base prices is a machine-learning and optimization stack that predicts how the Lyft marketplace responds to price, translates the cost of serving a ride into a price, and recommends price changes across hundreds of markets every week. Base prices are the foundation of every fare, and they set the reference point that dynamic pricing and rider discounts build on.
 The team serves two sets of customers: riders, who should see prices that are fair, competitive, and matched to what they value; and the analysts and market managers who use our models and tools to set pricing strategy.
 Responsibilities: 
 As the Staff Product Manager for Base Pricing, you will own the vision and roadmap for how Lyft sets base prices, and define the success metrics that measure it. That includes:
 Determining the optimal granularity at which Lyft sets base prices (e.g., by time, location, and type of trip)
 Improving how our base price optimization engine works with downstream dynamic pricing systems to better respond to real-time market conditions
 Re-evaluating how costs to fulfill a ride impact prices
 Jointly optimizing prices across ride types, so that standard, alternative modes, and scheduled rides are priced as one portfolio 
 Making our impact estimation models accurate and trusted by market management teams
 Evolving base pricing to function in a hybrid network with autonomous vehicles
 Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders (engineers, scientists, analysts), and partner teams (Driver Earnings, Verticals, Market Management) to align on a shared vision, define requirements, and prioritize inbound requests.
 Communicate roadmaps, experiment results, and pricing decisions clearly to audiences from partner teams up to Lyft's executive team.
 Experience: 
 8+ years of product management or relevant experience, with significant time spent on algorithmic, data-driven, pricing, or marketplace products
 A deep technical understanding of microeconomics, and ideally a background in Operations Research, Econometrics, Machine Learning, or algorithmic systems
 Experience owning pricing, revenue management, or other economic levers with direct P&L impact; experience with price optimization, elasticity modeling, or cost modeling is a strong plus
 Experience running A/B tests and market-level experiments, using statistical and causal inference techniques to evaluate results, and developing post-launch testing strategies
 Experience with data, including querying, aggregation, analysis, and visualization; comfortable working directly in SQL and with data science partners on model design
 Ability to define and analyze metrics that inform the success of products, and excellent judgment about the dynamics of a product ecosystem
 Natural ability to make things happen around you; you manage ambiguity, complexity, and interdependencies across many teams in an organized and structured way
 Strong communication skills and intuition for communication strategy at every level — within teams, within the company, and with executives
 Passion for Lyft and what we are trying to achieve in sustainable urban transportation

Sadie is building voice AI for hotels. When a guest calls, Sadie answers, day or night: it shares property information, quotes availability and rates, and books reservations in the hotel's own systems.
 We're looking for an early-career AI engineer to join our Montreal team and ship product work from your first weeks. The team is lean, so your code reaches real hotels quickly, and you'll be trusted with more as you prove yourself. Use AI to research, draft, test, and automate. You're responsible for the quality of the result.
 What you'll do
 Improve how the voice agent handles real calls 
 You'll review calls and transcripts to find where Sadie gets a request wrong, write the fix, and test it before it reaches a hotel. When Sadie fumbles a booking, the hotel hears about it from their guest.
 Build hotel system integrations 
 You'll build and maintain the connections that let Sadie check real availability and rates and write reservations back to the hotel. A mistake here means a double booking or a guest quoted the wrong price.
 Ship features and measure quality 
 You'll take features from idea to production and help build the test calls and checks that tell us whether a release made Sadie better or worse. Expect close code review, and to review others' code as you grow.
 What you'll bring
 You're graduating now, or graduated in the last one to two years.
 Either a FAANG internship, or startup experience or a project you built and shipped yourself.
 Clear evidence of initiative and strong ambition.
 Solid programming fundamentals and comfort building with LLMs and APIs.
 You work independently, ask for help early, and finish what you start.
 Useful experience
 A degree from a top Canadian university
 Hackathons, standout projects, or strong internships
 Voice or conversational AI work
 Who will enjoy this role
 Someone who hears a call that went wrong and can't let it go until it's fixed. The hard part: the team is small and moves quickly, so there's less hand-holding than at a large company, and your mistakes reach real guests.
 Why this role matters
 Small hotel teams miss calls, and each missed call can be a lost booking. As more hotels rely on Sadie, we need engineers who can own parts of the product. You'll start with well-defined pieces, and your scope will grow as fast as you do.

POSITION SUMMARY

The IT Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation, security, and continued maturity of North Vector Dynamics' internal information technology environment. This is a hands-on role: NVD currently manages its own IT in-house without a managed service provider, so the successful candidate will both set direction and do the work themselves. The role carries particular weight given NVD's status as a defence technology company operating under the Controlled Goods Program (CGP), the Document Security Control (DSC) program, and the Contract Security Program (CSP); IT decisions in this environment directly affect the company's ability to safeguard controlled goods, controlled technical data, and client information.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Infrastructure and Endpoint Management

• Own and maintain NVD's internal network, servers, endpoints, and cloud services.

• Establish and enforce a standardized device image and configuration baseline across company phones, laptops, and workstations, closing the current gap in automated patching and update management.

• Manage user account provisioning and deprovisioning, access permissions, and device inventory.

• Evaluate and recommend hardware, software, and infrastructure purchases in line with operational and budget needs.

Cybersecurity and Regulatory Compliance

• Act as the internal lead for NVD's Canadian Program for Cyber Security Certification (CPCSC) compliance work, coordinating with external consultants through Level 1 self-attestation and preparing the organization for an eventual Level 2 assessment.

• Implement and maintain technical controls required to protect controlled goods and controlled technical data consistent with NVD's CGP and DSC obligations.

• Maintain patch management, endpoint protection, backup, and disaster recovery processes, and remediate gaps identified through compliance reviews or audits.

• Support due diligence and compliance review of third-party software and platform vendors (for example, evaluating data sovereignty, export control, and information security posture of proposed tools) before they are adopted.

• Maintain documentation required to demonstrate compliance to auditors, customers, and government authorities.

Systems and Vendor Management

• Manage relationships with IT vendors, telecom providers, and software licensors, including contract renewals and cost review.

• Administer core business systems (email, file storage, CRM, website hosting and security, collaboration tools, and any engineering or telemetry platforms, private github, and any other IT tools required in the future) and manage integrations between them and develop SOPs, training and tutorials in support of new or existing tools.

• Support development and provide maintenance of on-premises AI server.

• Recommend and implement improvements to IT systems as the company scales.

IT Support and Operations

• Provide day-to-day technical support to staff across departments, resolving hardware, software, and connectivity issues.

• Maintain an asset register of company IT equipment, including issue and return of devices.

• Develop and maintain IT policies and procedures, including acceptable use, data handling, and incident response.

Reporting and Governance

• Report regularly to the Director of Operations on IT operations, security posture, outstanding risks, and compliance status.

• Escalate security incidents promptly and lead the internal response in coordination with company leadership.

• Support internal and external audits with accurate, timely documentation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

• Post-secondary education in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated experience.

• A minimum of 3 to 5 years of experience managing IT infrastructure, ideally including sole or lead responsibility for an organization's IT environment.

• Working knowledge of endpoint management, patch management, and standard network and cloud administration practices.

• Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, and the ability to meet the screening requirements of NVD's CGP registration and obtain a CSP security clearance.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical risk into terms leadership can act on.

Preferred

• Prior experience supporting cybersecurity certification frameworks such as CPCSC, CMMC, NIST 800-171, or ISO 27001.

• Experience working in a defence, aerospace, or other regulated/controlled-goods environment.

• Familiarity with export control considerations (for example, ITAR or Canadian export control regimes) as they relate to IT systems and data handling.

WORKING CONDITIONS

This position is based on-site at NVD's Calgary premises. Occasional after-hours availability may be required to respond to security incidents or system outages. The role involves handling controlled and sensitive information and is subject to NVD's internal security policies at all times.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

This is a Director-level individual contributor role, designed for an experienced leader who drives strategic impact through deep expertise, cross-functional influence, and ownership of key initiatives rather than direct people management.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, the Director of Product, AI Growth grows 1Password's new business in artificial intelligence. In this role, you own driving growth for our AI opportunities by identifying which customers we target, which outcomes we win on, and proving it with design customers. You scale growth through our go-to-market organization and through partnerships with the agent ecosystem and channel partners.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

What we're looking for:

 - Minimum of 8 years of product management experience, including experience carrying a revenue or adoption target, with a preference for experience in security products, agentic products, or developer tools.

 - Experience owning the strategy for a new product area or market entry, and taking it from hypothesis to customers running in production.

 - Experience working directly with enterprise customers on a technical deployment, as the person accountable for the outcome, and turning what those deployments proved into a repeatable motion a sales team can run.

 - Experience building technology partnerships and integrations, including judging where a product should sit in a larger technology ecosystem and working with business development on commercial terms.

 - Technical depth to hold a credible conversation with developers and security architects about how AI agents are built, deployed, and given access to systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to build alignment across go-to-market and engineering teams toward a shared goal, without direct authority over either.

 - Demonstrated ability to make decisions and move work forward with incomplete information in a fast-changing market.

 - Takes ownership end to end, including the work that falls between teams.

 - Works AI-first: uses agents in daily work, and applies their own judgement to decisions, product taste, and customer and internal relationships.

 - Preferred: familiarity with agentic access products, meaning the products that give AI agents credentials and access to the systems they work in.

What you can expect:

GROWTH STRATEGY

 - Own the growth thesis for 1Password's AI opportunities, covering the customer segments we target, the outcomes we deliver that we win on, and the workflows we get embedded into. Revise it as evidence arrives from customers, partners, and the market.

 - Form and test hypotheses using customer feedback, product usage data, partner input, and market research gathered with the go-to-market, product, user experience, and product marketing teams.

 - Lead a weekly business review that brings the voice of the customer, field feedback, and product usage telemetry into one view, so the team can refine targets, forecast the roadmap's impact on growth, and prioritize the blockers that hold adoption back.

 - Identify what stops customers from adopting, and drive each blocker to a resolution with the product team that owns it.

DESIGN CUSTOMER PROGRAM

 - Run the design customer program for new artificial intelligence opportunities, from selecting customers through to delivered outcomes.

 - Act as the general contractor for each design customer: the single person accountable for getting that customer deployed on 1Password for their agentic access, and for delivering the security and convenience outcomes they came for. Coordinate every team the deployment touches, and build what it requires together with a forward deployed engineering team.

 - Bring in solutions engineering, customer success, and product managers to help each customer reach their goal, and run feature betas with the product managers who own those features.

 - Turn what the program proves into the repeatable signal the company needs to scale, meaning the customer evidence, the deployment pattern, and the measured outcomes that the go-to-market and channel teams build sales plays on.

 - Improve the program each cycle so it reaches more design customers, raises delivery success rates and customer satisfaction, and shortens the time it takes the company to commercialize a new product.

PARTNERSHIPS

 - Decide where 1Password should play in the customer's artificial intelligence stack to deliver the most customer value in securing agent access. Agent access can be controlled at several points in that stack, so weigh those points and choose the ones that solve the most of the customer's problem, rather than the ones we fit into most easily. Base the call on how customers run AI today and on how the industry is evolving.

 - Identify and pursue the partnerships that let us play at those points and that complete an end-to-end customer outcome, meaning the outcome a customer cannot reach with 1Password alone.

 - Work with partners to deliver integrations, and find the patterns that let us repeat an integration across similar partners instead of building each one from scratch.

 - Work with the business development team to structure commercial relationships that grow both companies' business and deliver value to shared customers.

SCALE THROUGH THE FIELD AND THE DEVELOPER COMMUNITY

 - Work with product enablement to build demos and enablement content that the field and our channel partners can use without your involvement.

 - Work with developer relations to grow adoption organically among developers, through reference architectures, sample code, and open source contributions.

TRAVEL

 - Travel to design customer sites, partner meetings, and industry events approximately 10 to 20% of a given year.

About Faire 
 About this role: 
 Our Engineering organization owns the software that makes our marketplace work. Our Bot & Traffic Defence function owns how Faire holds up against automated traffic: scraping, credential abuse, and application-layer DDoS, from the edge through to detection and scoring. We care about good engineering practice and love to write software that is secure, tested, easy to maintain, and can scale to millions of users. We build scalable, reusable frameworks; consult with product teams; listen to the data; and iterate.
 As a Staff Security Engineer, Bot & Traffic Defence, you will be the first dedicated owner of this domain. You will set the technical direction, build the controls and signals that back it, and establish an ownership model that holds across Security, Platform, service teams, and Anti-Abuse.
 As a Staff Security Engineer, Bot & Traffic Defence, you’ll collaborate with us to: 
 Own the technical strategy and roadmap for bot, scraping, and application-layer DDoS defence end to end, from edge controls through detection and scoring, including revising the strategy where the evidence contradicts it.
 Author and tune edge security controls as code: WAF rules, rate limiting policies, and challenge mechanisms, against real adversaries who respond to every change you make.
 Build higher-confidence bot and trust signals so that Faire can enforce more aggressively without turning legitimate logged-out buyers away.
 Design and operate distributed layer 7 rate limiting, and make the calls on keying, counter state, and where in the stack enforcement belongs.
 Make incident response for bot and DDoS events a solved problem: clear paging paths, runbooks a non-specialist on-call can execute at 3am, and observability that answers whether humans are actually being affected.
 Lead post-incident reviews on recurring classes of bot incidents so systemic causes surface instead of repeating.
 Build the tooling, secure defaults, and playbooks that let service-owning teams protect their own endpoints correctly without you in the loop for every decision.
 Land a durable ownership model across Security, Platform, service teams, and Anti-Abuse, where every attack vector has a named owner who has accepted it and it holds without escalation.
 Make Faire's bot posture legible to leadership, including a defensible view of residual risk, and force the outstanding business decisions that engineering is currently making by default.
 We’re excited about you because you have: 
 Hands-on operational ownership of a CDN or edge security platform (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, or AWS CloudFront/WAF/Shield) in production against real adversaries, managed as code rather than clicked through a vendor dashboard.
 Experience defending a high-traffic consumer site against scraping and application-layer DDoS, including the part where the attacker shifts vectors a week after your control ships, and the instinct to design for raising attacker cost rather than for a permanent block.
 A practical understanding of bot detection signals and where each one fails: TLS and HTTP fingerprinting (JA3/JA4), behavioural signals, mobile device attestation (App Attest, Play Integrity), and challenges, with a real view on the precision and recall trade-off each one carries.
 Experience designing distributed rate limiting at layer 7, including the differences between per-IP, per-ASN, per-session, and per-fingerprint keying, when each gets evaded, and how to hold counter state across a fleet without the limiter becoming the bottleneck.
 Quantitative rigour in detection work: you can measure a detection's precision and recall, set a false-positive tolerance with the business, and defend a threshold change with data rather than intuition.
 A preference for solving traffic and abuse problems with code rather than manual operations, including writing and maintaining internal tooling that on-call engineers depend on mid-incident.
 Comfort writing and reviewing code in an OOP language such as Kotlin, Java, Python, or TypeScript, enough to read an unfamiliar service, find where a control is being bypassed, and open the pull request that fixes it.
 Working fluency with infrastructure as code and cloud environments (Terraform, AWS or GCP, Kubernetes) sufficient to own a security control plane, and the judgment to know when a Terraform-gated workflow is too slow for an incident and needs a break-glass path with an audit trail.
 Experience owning incident response for a live traffic attack, including holding the authority to block traffic under time pressure.
 A track record of setting technical direction in an ambiguous domain with no existing owner, and of sequencing work when everything is nominally urgent.
 Experience landing a cross-team ownership model without authority, including moving responsibility away from a team that currently holds it and getting other teams to accept obligations they did not ask for.
 Comfort delivering primarily through other teams rather than personal throughput.
 The ability to put security risk in business terms for executives, translating traffic and abuse metrics into revenue, cost, and reputational exposure.
 Clear communication with engineers outside security, describing an attack and its trade-offs without alarmism or unexplained jargon.
 Technologies we use and teach: 
 Kotlin, Typescript, Python
 Edge and CDN security tooling: WAF, rate limiting, bot management, challenge policies
 AWS, OCI, Terraform, Kubernetes
 HTTP, JSON, and Protocol Buffers

You'll work directly with the founder on whatever business problem matters most at Aran.
 This is intentionally a broad role. We're early enough that drawing hard lines between sales, business development, partnerships, operations, recruiting, and strategy would slow us down.
 Your initial focus will be customers and revenue: finding the companies building the world's largest data centers and industrial projects, getting Aran in the room, turning their problems into projects, closing the purchase order, and growing those relationships over time.
 Our founder leads sales today. You'll own deals and make sure every one of them keeps moving.
 But that won't be the whole job.
 One week you might be working through procurement with a customer to get a project signed. The next you might build an internal tool the whole team ends up using, help build a partnership with an equipment manufacturer, recruit someone exceptional, prepare for an investor or customer meeting, or solve an operational problem nobody has owned yet.
 There is no playbook and there won't always be someone telling you what to do next. You'll find the highest-leverage problem, own it, and keep pushing until it's solved.
 We're building a very small team capable of doing what traditionally required entire organizations. That applies to the business side of Aran just as much as the engineering side.
 How you'll work 
 You run the whole loop yourself:
 Find what matters. Figure out where your time can have the highest impact on the company right now.
 Get into the details. Talk to customers, engineers, partners, candidates, investors, or whoever has the context you need. Understand the actual problem rather than operating from a distance.
 Own it. Develop the strategy, do the work, coordinate whoever needs to be involved, and drive it to an outcome.
 Close the loop. A customer conversation should turn into a proposal. A proposal should turn into a PO. A successful project should turn into another project. An operational headache should turn into a system that prevents it from happening again.

Ashby's GTM engine runs on a set of interconnected systems. Keeping them accurate, efficient, and trusted is the foundation everything else is built on. As our GTM Systems Analyst, you'll own the daily maintenance and configuration of technical layer that powers our Go-to-Market organization: the CRM configurations, integration architecture, and data quality practices that let our Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams move fast with confidence.

This role sits within Revenue Operations, the horizontal function that makes the entire GTM system work. You'll be embedded in daily operations (triaging issues, implementing new tooling, and translating business requirements into scalable configurations) while also contributing to longer-term systems strategy as we move up-market and expand our product suite.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS NOW

We're in an active expansion phase: new products, new segments, new GTM motions. Our systems need to keep pace. The person in this role will shape how we build the technical foundation for the next chapter of Ashby's growth.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - System Administration: Own the day-to-day health of our core GTM platforms. You'll manage configuration, user permissions, custom objects, and workflow automation across our CRM stack — making sure the systems actually reflect how our teams work, not just how they were set up two years ago.

 - Integration Support: Maintain clean data flows across our GTM toolset ( including intent data, conversation intelligence, and sales engagement platforms). You'll be the person who knows how signals travel between systems and why, and who makes sure they're flowing reliably.

 - Data Governance: Enforce standards for data quality, deduplication, and field taxonomy. Revenue reporting and forecasting are only as good as the data underneath them, along with our GTM Engineers and our System Architect, you'll build the infrastructure of trust that makes those outputs credible.

 - Stakeholder Support: Be the go-to technical partner for frontline GTM teams. You'll triage issues, gather business requirements, and deliver solutions that scale.  - Tooling Evaluation: Help evaluate new GTM tech and AI tools as our needs evolve. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience connecting marketing automation, CRM, and revenue intelligence tools (e.g., 6sense, Gong, Outreach, Gainsight)

You’ll combine security engineering and automation to strengthen authentication and authorization, enforce least privilege, and simplify identity lifecycle management across our infrastructure.  Automate identity lifecycle processes to ensure access is granted, modified, and revoked promptly.

À propos de Mila 
 Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions au domaine de l’apprentissage profond, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
 Sommaire du poste
 Le Laboratoire d'IA souveraine est une nouvelle initiative de Mila visant à assembler une pile (stack) d'inférence en IA open source, prête pour l'entreprise, que les organisations peuvent déployer et exploiter sur des infrastructures qu'elles contrôlent. Elle regroupe des fonctionnalités telles que la mise en service de modèles (model serving), la recherche d'information (retrieval), l'orchestration d'agents, l'observabilité et un plan de contrôle (control plane) pour opérer ces composants comme un produit cohérent.
 En tant que gestionnaire senior de la livraison technique, vous dirigerez la livraison de bout en bout des déploiements partenaires, depuis la découverte initiale et l'étude de faisabilité jusqu'à la planification, le déploiement, le transfert opérationnel et la revue d'adoption initiale. Vous gérerez plusieurs pilotes et déploiements en production simultanés, en servant de point de contact et de responsabilité principal auprès du partenaire durant la phase active de livraison. Relevant du directeur principal du produit, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'ingénierie et les partenariats pour définir des engagements crédibles, coordonner l'exécution et maintenir l'alignement entre les parties prenantes techniques et exécutives.
 Il s'agit d'un rôle de coordination à forte maîtrise technique. Vous définirez la portée de livraison, les jalons, les responsabilités, les risques et les critères d'acceptation; vous coordonnerez les développeurs et spécialistes réalisant le travail; et vous recommanderez des ajustements lorsque la portée, l'échéancier ou le niveau de préparation ne seront plus réalistes.
 Le succès signifie que les partenaires réalisent des déploiements opérationnels validés selon les critères d'acceptation convenus, commencent à adopter la pile pour leurs cas d'usage visés et sont prêts à l'exploiter. Cela signifie également que chaque déploiement génère des enseignements produits exploitables et améliore les guides pratiques (playbooks), les critères d'acceptation et les pratiques de livraison utilisés avec les futurs partenaires.
 Principales responsabilités
 Mener la phase de découverte initiale auprès des partenaires afin de comprendre le cas d'usage visé, l'environnement de déploiement, les contraintes organisationnelles et les critères de succès, en collaboration avec l'ingénierie pour évaluer la faisabilité avant la prise d'engagements.
 Définir et maintenir les plans de livraison à travers plusieurs déploiements partenaires simultanés, incluant la portée, les jalons, les responsabilités, les dépendances, les besoins en ressources, les risques et les critères d'acceptation.
 Agir en tant que responsable principal vis-à-vis du partenaire durant la livraison active, en communiquant l'avancement, les décisions, les risques et les changements aux équipes techniques et aux sponsors exécutifs.
 Servir de pont principal entre notre équipe interne et l'équipe du partenaire de déploiement tout au long du processus de mise en œuvre.
 Identifier rapidement les risques de livraison et les décisions non tranchées, évaluer leurs implications et recommander des ajustements de portée, de séquence, d'échéancier ou de préparation lorsque les engagements ne sont plus crédibles.
 Mener des sessions de rétroaction structurées avec les administrateurs et utilisateurs des partenaires, en traduisant les constats du déploiement et les retours en problématiques produit et en recommandations.
 Repérer les tendances à travers les déploiements et élaborer des guides pratiques (playbooks), modèles, critères d'acceptation et pratiques de revue réutilisables afin d'améliorer les livraisons futures.
